clips.text: Once a year, your pension sends you a letter. It's long, and it looks important. Here's what it actually says.
First, it tells you how much is in your pot today. That's everything you've saved so far.
Then, what went in this year. That's your money, plus whatever your employer added on top.
Next comes a guess at what you might get each year, when you retire. It's an estimate. Not a promise.
So what do you need to do? Usually, nothing at all. Check your name and address are right, and keep it somewhere safe.
And if anything looks wrong, ring the number on the letter. That's exactly what it's there for.
